paper_metadata.title: Efficient option pricing with unary-based photonic computing chip and generative adversarial learning

summary: The paper demonstrates a silicon photonic chip implementing a unary quantum option-pricing pipeline with distribution loading, payoff rotation, and iterative amplitude estimation. A proof-of-principle experiment prices a European option with 3 discretized asset values (6 waveguides) and up to 50 amplitude-estimation iterations, reducing payoff estimation standard deviation from ~0.2 to <0.004 over repeated measurements. A hybrid photonic–classical GAN is also trained on-chip to learn 8-bin log-normal and normal distributions, reaching an ℓ2 error of about −18 dB after ~100 training iterations.

experiments.description: Photonic-chip implementation of unary European option pricing with distribution loading, payoff calculation, and iterative amplitude estimation for a 3-asset / 3-bin proof-of-principle case.

algorithm.variant: Unary option pricing with iterative amplitude estimation (without phase estimation)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Repeated amplitude amplification steps up to m=50 to improve payoff estimation accuracy

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Continuous asset-price distribution is binned into a unary basis; each bin is represented by a waveguide mode, with an additional ancilla waveguide per bin to emulate the ancilla qubit. For the 3-asset example, 6 waveguides are used.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the expected European option payoff C(ST,K)=∫_K^∞(ST-K)dST via measurement of the ancilla state |1⟩ after payoff rotation and amplitude estimation.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection / measurement of ancilla waveguides encoding state |1⟩; unary mapping avoids non-local controlled gates.

problem_instance.description: European option pricing on a photonic chip, proof-of-principle with three asset values; distribution loading demonstrated on 8 bins for GAN training, and option pricing demonstrated on 3 asset values.

dataset_specification.description: Market data used to define target log-normal and normal distributions for GAN training; no ticker/date range specified.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Asset-price distribution is discretized into bins; for the GAN, target distributions are log-normal and normal examples. The paper states the GAN captures the probability distribution underlying market data, but does not specify a detailed preprocessing pipeline.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Amplitude estimation performance evaluated over increasing m; 50 measurements performed in each step of amplitude estimation; GAN training shown over 100 iterations.

quantum_resources.readout_fidelity: SNSPD efficiency 85% (detector efficiency), dark counts 100 Hz

hardware.provider: Advanced Micro Foundry (fabrication) / A*STAR IME collaboration

noise_model.noise_type: photonic experimental imperfections, crosstalk, detector noise
noise_model.error_mitigation_method: post-selection strategy for unary scheme; GAN training incorporates chip imperfections
noise_model.noise_parameters: SNSPD dark counts 100 Hz; detector efficiency 85%
noise_model.mitigation_details: Post-selection strategy mentioned for error mitigation; no further quantitative mitigation protocol reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: GAN discriminator implemented classically in TensorFlow; generator trained with evolutionary optimization and Wasserstein distance
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measured ancilla probabilities converted to payoff estimate; raw angles shifted back to original angles in analysis

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: payoff error and standard deviation decrease with increasing amplitude-estimation iterations; GAN training converges over 100 iterations

speedup_claims.conditions: iterative amplitude estimation without phase estimation; in terms of number of calls to D and P operators / number of quantum samples
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports a proof-of-principle photonic implementation and states the asymptotic scaling O(1/sqrt(m)) versus O(1/m) for Monte Carlo; exact wall-clock speedup is not reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/√m) scaling of error with quantum samples; quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo in number of calls to D and P operators
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(1/m) for Monte Carlo convergence as stated in the paper's comparison

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not estimated; current demonstration limited to 3 bins / asset values.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Large-scale photonic processor capable of representing many bins (high-dimensional qudit states) and executing many amplitude amplification iterations with low loss and high detection efficiency.
limiting_factors: Quadratic speedup from amplitude estimation only
No classical runtime benchmark on realistic financial datasets
Unary encoding scales linearly in hardware resources (waveguides)
Photon loss and detector noise limit scaling
Distribution loading overhead may dominate runtime

notes: The paper reports a photonic chip with 6 waveguide inputs for the 3-asset proof-of-principle, but does not state a qubit count explicitly; num_qubits is inferred from the unary encoding plus ancilla structure and therefore left as null in the strict qubit sense.
Circuit depth is described qualitatively as linear depth for distribution loading and repeated amplitude amplification up to m=50, but no exact compiled depth is given.
The paper claims quadratic speedup over Monte Carlo due to amplitude estimation but demonstrates only a small proof-of-principle with three asset values.
No empirical comparison with classical runtimes on meaningful financial problem sizes.

experiments.description: On-chip generative adversarial network training to learn and load target asset-price distributions into the photonic unary encoder, demonstrated on log-normal and normal distributions with up to 8 bins.

algorithm.variant: Hybrid GAN with photonic generator and classical discriminator
algorithm.optimizer: evolutionary optimization for generator; gradient descent for discriminator
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Training complete when generator fools discriminator / Wasserstein critic stabilizes; reported over 100 iterations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Probability distribution is encoded into waveguide occupation probabilities of the unary basis; generator parameters are phase shifters on the photonic chip.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Learn a generator distribution matching the target market distribution using GAN/Wasserstein training.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Wasserstein critic used to stabilize GAN training; generator optimized with gradient-free evolutionary algorithm due to stochastic measurements.

problem_instance.description: Distribution learning / loading for asset-price distributions used by the option-pricing pipeline.

dataset_specification.description: Target distributions are log-normal and normal examples derived from market-data-inspired samples; no explicit dataset name or ticker list given.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Real samples are drawn from the desired probability distribution; fake samples are photon occupation probabilities across waveguide modes.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of generated and target distributions; ℓ2 norm tracked over 100 training iterations for both log-normal and normal cases.

quantum_resources.readout_fidelity: SNSPD efficiency 85% (detector efficiency), dark counts 100 Hz

hardware.provider: Advanced Micro Foundry (fabrication) / A*STAR IME collaboration
hardware.framework: TensorFlow for classical discriminator; photonic chip control not otherwise specified

noise_model.noise_type: photonic experimental imperfections and stochastic measurement noise
noise_model.error_mitigation_method: Wasserstein GAN training and evolutionary optimization to handle stochastic gradients
noise_model.noise_parameters: SNSPD dark counts 100 Hz; detector efficiency 85%
noise_model.mitigation_details: Hybrid training strategy with gradient-free generator optimization and Wasserstein critic

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical discriminator implemented in TensorFlow; real samples from target distributions; evolutionary algorithm used for generator training
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: ℓ2 norm between fake and real distributions computed to assess convergence

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: monotonic convergence of ℓ2 norm over training iterations

speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or empirical speedup is claimed for the GAN training module itself; the paper’s speedup claim pertains to the amplitude-estimation option-pricing module.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not applicable — experiment demonstrates distribution learning on photonic hardware but does not benchmark against classical GAN training cost.
limiting_factors: Hybrid training dominated by classical discriminator
Unclear scaling of photonic generator parameters

notes: The paper explicitly describes a photonic generator and classical discriminator, but does not state a qubit count; the photonic implementation is therefore treated as physical hardware with qubit count not explicitly reported.
No asymptotic speedup is claimed for the GAN training itself; the speedup claim in the paper pertains to the amplitude-estimation option-pricing module, not the GAN.
The GAN component is presented as a method for loading probability distributions into the photonic circuit rather than demonstrating computational advantage.
No performance comparison with classical generative models.
